subject: zoology_2
question_text: Explain the different types of cancers.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.43, SAQ 45. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revision (examiner audit, 2026-09-05): the printed heading 'Based on their origin' ran over all six numbered types, but items 5 and 6 are grouped by family history, so a second heading was added before item 5 and the insider note was corrected to match.

steps.label: Carcinoma and sarcoma
steps.why: Epithelium covers every surface of the body and divides constantly, which is why cancers of it are the commonest kind.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two. Carcinoma is epithelial, sarcoma is connective tissue.
Leaving out that carcinoma is the most common.
steps.memory_tip: Carcinoma covers surfaces; sarcoma sits in connective tissue.
steps.margin_note: Say the classification is by origin.

steps.label: Leukemia
steps.why: The cancer cells stay in the blood instead of forming a lump, which is why it is called a liquid tumour.
common_mistakes: Calling leukemia a solid tumour. It is a liquid tumour.
Naming the wrong cells. It is the white blood cells.
steps.memory_tip: Leukemia is blood cancer: a liquid tumour.
steps.margin_note: Name the tissue and the cells.

steps.label: Lymphoma
steps.why: The lymphatic system runs through the whole body, so a cancer of it can appear in many places at once.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the system it affects.
steps.memory_tip: Lymphoma is cancer of the lymphatic system.

steps.label: Familial and sporadic
steps.why: These two are not named by tissue but by whether the risk was inherited, so they cut across the other four.
common_mistakes: Treating familial and sporadic as tissue types.
Naming only one of the two.
steps.memory_tip: Familial runs in the family; sporadic appears out of nowhere.
steps.margin_note: Close with the two that depend on family history.

lines.text: 6. Sporadic cancer: with no family history

insider_note: Four types are named by the tissue they start in — epithelial, connective, bone marrow and lymphatic. The last two, familial and sporadic, are named by family history instead.
